title: Client-side and server-side validation: why you need both

videos.script: A sign-up form says the name is required. It says the e-mail needs an at sign. It says nobody is born next year. {{form}} The browser enforces all of it, before anything is sent. {{browser}} Now send the same request without the browser. One line of curl. {{curl}} The server answers welcome, and stores an empty name, an address with no at sign, and a birth date five years away. {{welcome}} The browser's checks were never a control. They belong to whoever holds the browser. {{whose}} They are still worth having. They make the form quicker to fill in. But the check that decides what gets stored lives on the server. {{server}} Today you move every rule to the server, and draw the form from the same rules, so the two can never disagree. {{one}}
